limitations: The supplied record is normalized advisory evidence rather than an executable trace.
The available finding text does not define a public detector implementation, its complete source/sink catalog, taint semantics, dominance model, or validation recognizers.
Local API-pattern matching can observe calls but cannot decide URI provenance, canonical target identity, provider behavior, permissions, storage accessibility, or copy success.
predicates: A URI originates from an external or otherwise less-trusted boundary.
That URI, or a path derived from it, reaches a source-opening or source-copy operation.
The resulting bytes reach a destination rooted in app-specific external storage.
No effective validation evidence restricts the resolved source away from protected internal application data on all successful paths.
detector_semantics.claim: The finding claims a potential insufficient-validation/confused-deputy pattern: externally originating URI data can influence a privileged source read and a copy into external storage.

unknowns: No public detector-rule catalog or CrySL artifact defining PathValidationSpec was supplied or identified; therefore its label cannot be expanded into a named governed API type.
The precise matching, taint propagation, sanitizer recognition, and path-sensitivity behavior of the detector are not available from the normalized finding.
The exact URI scheme and target resource used by any later finding are unknown.
The exact deployment environment determining external-storage readability is unknown.
The finding alone does not reveal whether the source bytes were sensitive, whether copying completed, or whether any other application accessed the resulting file.

The relationship between the concern label and a specific CWE mapping remains descriptive rather than definitive: the directly linked advisory lists CWE-441 and CWE-610, while CWE-22 is related generic pathname guidance rather than a verified universal mapping.

documented_behavior: ContentResolver.openInputStream(Uri) opens an InputStream for content, android.resource, or file URIs; it can throw FileNotFoundException and can return null if the provider recently crashed.
Uri exposes decoded scheme and path components, but those accessors do not establish the identity, authorization, or safety of the resource ultimately opened.

Context.getExternalFilesDir(String) returns an app-specific directory on shared/external storage and may return null when that storage is unavailable. FileOutputStream(File) opens the supplied File for writing or throws when it cannot be opened.

File canonicalization resolves pathname equivalence such as redundant dot segments and, typically on Unix, symbolic links; this is pathname behavior, not proof that an opened descriptor remains the same object after a check. Android ContentResolver guidance distinguishes safe descriptor validation from URI reuse.
Apache Commons IO provides the observed copy helpers: IOUtils copies between streams and FileUtils copies file contents to a destination.
preconditions: The receiving code must accept an externally supplied URI.
The app must be able to open the URI or successfully execute one of the file-path fallback branches.
External storage must be available and the destination File must be creatable and writable.
The selected copy helper must complete successfully for source bytes to reach the destination.
unknowns: Which URI schemes, authorities, grant flags, and provider implementations are accepted by the analyzed build.
Whether source validation exists outside the local reported slice or dominates every successful resolution and fallback branch.
Which Apache Commons IO version is packaged by the analyzed artifact and whether helper behavior differs from current documentation.
Whether any path helper transforms, canonicalizes, rejects, or otherwise constrains URI-derived paths.

events.condition: Observed when ContentResolver.openInputStream is invoked. The security predicate requires data flow from an externally controlled URI to this argument and successful resolution to a source that the caller is authorized to read; the call alone does not prove its scheme, provider, resolved object, or successful read.
events.name: uri_resolved_as_input

events.condition: Observed when URI path material, directly or through a path helper, is converted to a File and supplied to a file-copy operation. The security predicate requires that this derived path resolves to a protected or policy-disallowed source and that no effective check constrains that resolved source on the executed branch.
events.name: uri_path_used_as_file_source

events.condition: Observed when a File under the app-specific external-files directory is selected and opened for writing. The security predicate requires that this is the destination receiving the sensitive source bytes and that the deployed Android/storage configuration permits a less-trusted principal to read that destination; the directory API call alone does not prove cross-app readability.
events.name: external_destination_created

events.condition: Observed when a recognized stream or file copy helper is called. The security predicate requires a successful copy from the resolved source to the external destination; invocation alone does not prove that bytes were transferred, committed, retained, or later exposed.
events.name: bytes_copied_to_destination

important_note: PathValidationSpec is a concern label, not a governed API type, CrySL rule, or published detector-rule name. The relevant advisory describes uncontrolled URI-based content resolution and lists CWE-441 and CWE-610; it does not establish that every finding is conventional CWE-22 traversal. Android security guidance separately identifies untrusted file:// URIs passed to ContentResolver as a confused-deputy risk.
forbidden_inferences_without_evidence: That PathValidationSpec names a Java/Kotlin class, a platform API type, a CrySL rule, or a public detector-catalog rule.
That a similarly named type from another framework governs this concern.
That the URI uses the file scheme, points to internal application data, or resolves to any particular canonical path.
That a call to ContentResolver.openInputStream succeeds, returns a non-null stream, or reads bytes from the expected object.
That a source-level check is effective across all successful branches, including URI-path fallback branches.
That an external-files destination is readable by every other application on every Android version, target SDK, device configuration, or permission state.
That a static/advisory finding proves exploitability, successful copying, data sensitivity, or observed runtime exfiltration.
That the representative advisory's affected-version information applies to a different artifact, variant, commit, dependency set, or deployed build.
That the CROSSINGTUD corpus is evidence for this specification.

security_semantics.runtime_claim: A security impact requires additional facts: an attacker can supply the relevant URI; resolution or fallback accesses protected data using the app's authority; copying succeeds; and the resulting destination is accessible to a less-trusted principal. Android documents untrusted file URI use with ContentResolver as capable of exposing protected data, but platform conditions remain material.
security_semantics.detector_claim: A potentially less-trusted URI controls a resource reference that the app resolves with its own access and then copies toward external storage; this matches the advisory's uncontrolled-content-resolution framing and the confused-deputy/resource-reference CWE concepts.

compatibility: The exact application artifact, variant, commit, and dependency lock state corresponding to the reported source tag.
The Android API level and target SDK used at runtime.
The ContentProvider implementation and URI-permission behavior for each tested URI.
The Apache Commons IO version and behavior bundled with the artifact.
runtime: The actual incoming URI string, scheme, authority, grant state, and originating component.
The opened descriptor or canonical source identity, including whether it refers to protected application data.
Successful copy completion and byte-level correspondence between source and destination.
The device API level, target SDK, storage mode, installed permissions, and a concrete demonstration of whether another principal can read the destination.
source_level: A source-to-sink data-flow trace from an externally controlled URI to ContentResolver.openInputStream(Uri) or to a File created from URI-derived path material.
Evidence that the input stream or file-copy source reaches the same destination opened below Context.getExternalFilesDir(String).
Evidence about all successful primary and fallback branches, including the stream-copy branch and URI-path-derived FileUtils.copyFile branches.
Evidence that any source restriction is absent or ineffective for the resolved source on every relevant successful branch.

name: PathValidationSpec
source_title: Uncontrolled data used in content resolution — GHSA-g38r-4cf6-3v32 / CVE-2023-33188
semantic_scope: For every finding of this rule, the detector observes or normalizes a potential static/advisory flow in which an externally supplied URI may be resolved using the receiving app's authority and copied, directly or through a URI-path fallback, to an app-specific external-storage destination without evidence in the finding record of an effective source-identity restriction. It is not a runtime log and does not itself establish URI control, protected-source resolution, byte transfer, destination readability, or exploitability.
known_false_positive_shapes: The URI is constructed solely from a trusted in-process source and cannot be influenced by an external sender.
A dominating, effective policy check rejects protected or disallowed resolved sources on every primary and fallback branch, but local matching does not recognize that check.
The URI is a provider-backed content URI whose provider and URI grants restrict access to only intended non-sensitive content.
The resolver open fails, returns no usable stream, and every fallback copy path also fails before bytes are written.
The external destination is not readable by a less-trusted principal in the actual Android version, target-SDK, permission, and storage configuration.
The copied data is non-sensitive and the security policy permits its placement in that destination.
protocol: externally supplied URI? → resolve/read via ContentResolver.openInputStream(uri) or URI-path-derived File fallback → create destination below Context.getExternalFilesDir(...) → FileOutputStream(destination) → stream/file byte copy

detector_examples.message: External finding (CVE-2023-33188): createExternalStoragePrivateFile copies an externally supplied URI into external attachment storage without validating whether the source refers to protected internal app data. Source tag: 6.1.0. This is a normalized advisory record, not a runtime log.

source_audit.detail: none of the specification's findings mention org.apache.commons.io.IOUtils, org.apache.commons.io.FileUtils
